subject: Client cabinet, identity checks, customer ledger, TradeLocker interface
body:
Portal is now a broker client area with left-hand tabs - Dashboard, Funds,
Identity, Partner, Settings - instead of a page of cards, on a brighter
palette. /partner redirects into it.

Identity checks:
- Documents are stored in Postgres (15 GB disk, a few MB used), so they
  survive a redeploy unlike a container filesystem, behind storage columns
  that make a later move to object storage a backfill not a migration.
- Type is sniffed from the leading bytes, never from Content-Type: an
  executable renamed to .jpg is refused. 6 MB cap, raw body, no multipart
  dependency to keep in sync with the deploy repo's manifest.
- A customer is approved only when every document is; one rejection holds
  the whole check. Documents are served inline with nosniff, staff only.

The ledger:
- Append-only. A balance is always derived by summing it, never stored on
  the user row, so no second number can drift.
- Only confirmed rows count. A deposit that was seen but not confirmed is
  not spendable - that is how a sibling brand credited ~$64k that never
  arrived.
- A unique index on `reference` means the same transaction hash cannot be
  credited twice; the second attempt is refused, not silently doubled.
- Requesting a withdrawal debits immediately under a row lock, so the same
  balance cannot be withdrawn twice while an admin decides, and nothing
  leaves without an approved identity check.
- Rejecting posts ONE compensating credit. The first version also reversed
  the original debit, which handed the money back twice and turned a
  balance of 300 into 700 on every rejected withdrawal. Caught by the test
  that asserts the balance returns to exactly what it was.

TradeLocker sits behind a TradingPlatform interface and stays disabled
until TRADELOCKER_* is set. The client is written but UNVERIFIED against
live credentials, and status() reports configured/reachable separately so
nothing can claim a connection that was never made.

Markets section lists all 54 instruments grouped by class, with no invented
prices. One-line logo with a new mark. Footer states plainly that the US is
not served, alongside the risk warning.

Verified: 99 checks against the live database across auth, back office,
partners and money.
